problem_motivation.content: High strength and ductility are often mutually exclusive properties in structural materials.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: High strength and ductility, often mutually exclusive properties of a structural material, are also responsible for damage tolerance.

problem_motivation.content: The origin of the excellent properties of High Entropy Alloy (HEA) nanowires is not yet understood, hindering their design and application.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Therefore, understanding the origin of such excellent properties is an important scientific issue for the design and application of HEA NWs.

prior_approach.content: Otto et al. reported increased yield strength and elongation with decreasing temperature in CoNiCrFeMn alloy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Otto et al. [ [18] ] reported an increment in the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and elongation to fracture with decreasing temperature especially in the cryogenic range.

prior_approach.content: Xiao et al. performed MD simulations on CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires at room temperature.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Xiao et al. [ [23] ] inflicted tensile deformation on CoNiCrFeMn HEA NWs using MD simulations at room temperature

prior_approach.content: Deng et al. performed MD simulations on periodically twinned FCC nanowires to study plasticity transitions.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Deng et al. [ [33] ] performed an MD simulation on periodically twinned FCC NWs and found a fundamental transition of plasticity from a sharp yield point and strain softening to significant strain hardening as stacking fault energy (SFE) of the metal decreases.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have reported similar deformation behaviors and serration effects in metallic nanowires.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This behavior is reported in numerous studies [ [7] , [8] , [9] , [10] ] related to deformation in metallic nanowires.

prior_limitation.content: In HEA nanowires, partial dislocation motion is hindered by friction due to lattice parameter differences, leading to hardening and reduced ductility.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: In high entropy alloy (HEA) CoNiCrFeMn nanowires, the motion of the partial dislocation is hindered by the friction due to difference in the lattice parameter of the constituent atoms which is responsible for the hardening and lowering the ductility.

inspiration_source.content: The selection of silver nanowires is based on the reported dependence of dislocation and twinning nucleation on stacking fault energy in metals.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Further, it has also been reported that the nucleation of dislocation and twinning is often dependent on stacking fault energy in the metals.

causal_claim.content: Mechanical properties of HEA nanowires are superior to Ag nanowires because of synergistic interactions between deformation twinning, phase transformation, and cross-section reorientation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Mechanical properties of HEA nanowires are better than Ag nanowires due to synergistic interactions of deformation twinning, FCC-HCP phase transformation, and the special reorientation of the cross-section.

causal_claim.content: Thermal vibrations retard twin boundary propagation and prevent complete phase transformation at elevated temperatures.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At elevated temperatures, the propagation of twin boundaries is retarded due to thermal vibrations and complete transformation from (110) to (100) phase is not possible.

causal_claim.content: Lomer Cottrell locks hinder dislocation motion, leading to enhanced work hardening.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These Lomer Cottrell locks further act to hinder dislocation motion on the slip planes, resulting in enhanced work hardening.

causal_claim.content: The synergistic activation of multiple mechanisms provides high strength, ductility, and work hardening in HEA NWs.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The synergistic effect of these mechanisms provides exceptional strength, ductility, increased work hardening rate and damage tolerance to the HEA NW.

mechanism_principle.content: Plasticity at different stages and temperatures is caused by the simultaneous activation of twinning induced plasticity and transformation induced plasticity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Further examination reveals that simultaneous activation of twining induced plasticity and transformation induced plasticity are responsible for the plasticity at different stages and temperatures.

mechanism_principle.content: Phase transformation from FCC to HCP is driven by stacking fault energy and the formation of intrinsic stacking faults.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The FCC-HCP transformation often takes place with the aid of stacking faults.

hypothesis_statement.content: The findings suggest potential utility for designing nanowires with high stability and superior mechanical properties for the semiconductor industry.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: These findings could be very useful for designing nanowires at different temperatures with high stability and superior mechanical properties in the semiconductor industry.

hypothesis_statement.content: Silver nanowires will exhibit deformation behaviors similar to CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires due to their comparable stacking fault energies.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Therefore, we have chosen silver (Ag) nanowires which have similar SFEs to the CoNiCrFeMn HEAs.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors speculate that local chemical composition variations in the HEA facilitate the formation of Lomer Cottrell locks.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We speculate that variations in the local chemical composition in HEA nanowires facilitate the formation of Lomer Cottrell locks

evidence_result.content: Ag nanowires exhibit temperature-dependent superplasticity at cryogenic temperatures due to cross-section reorientation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The results demonstrate that Ag nanowires exhibit apparent temperature-dependent superplasticity at cryogenic temperature due to (110) to (100) cross-section reorientation behavior.

evidence_result.content: HEA nanowires show exceptional strength-ductility trade-offs at cryogenic temperatures and maintain good properties at high temperatures.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Interestingly, HEA nanowires can perform exceptional strength-ductility trade-offs at cryogenic temperatures. Even at high temperatures, HEA nanowires can still maintain good flow stress and ductility prior to failure.

evidence_result.content: Measured stress-strain curves show two distinct peaks for Ag NWs at 77K, corresponding to phase re-orientation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 2 shows the stress–strain curves of the Ag NWs and CoNiCrFeMn HEA NWs at 77, 300, and 1000 K respectively.

evidence_result.content: The stress-strain curve for CoNiCrFeMn HEA NW shows a drop in stress indicating twin formation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: After a succession of such events in HEA NW, a remarkable drop in stress indicates the formation of deformation twins

evidence_result.content: Quantitative data shows the fraction of HCP atoms increases with strain, confirming martensitic transformation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 8 a shows the fraction of atoms in different phases at 77 K with increasing strain.

evidence_result.content: Experimental data indicates higher HCP phase fractions at 1000K compared to lower temperatures.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Interestingly, the fraction of HCP atoms at 1000 K is much higher than 77 and 300 K in the later stage of deformation as can be seen in Figure 8 b.
